html:
Slobodan Milošević was the leader of Serbia from 1989 to 2000, born in 1941 in Požarevac in eastern Serbia, whose nationalist policies did much to drive the breakup of Yugoslavia and the wars that followed.

A communist banker and party official, he rose in 1987 by championing Serbs in Kosovo and ended the province's autonomy in 1989. When Slovenia and Croatia left Yugoslavia, he backed Serb rebels in Croatia and Bosnia. He signed the Dayton Agreement in 1995, then fought the Kosovo War against NATO in 1999. He was overthrown in 2000 and sent to the tribunal in The Hague, where he died in his cell before a verdict.
